open_findings.expected: OWNER-CHECKPOINT: the one owner action is presented, and the email is entered only at a visible, non-echoing prompt.
open_findings.minimal_repair: Write the prompt to the terminal, not stderr: `printf 'Owner email (not echoed): ' >/dev/tty; read -r -s value </dev/tty; printf '\n' >/dev/tty; printf '%s' "$value"`. Optionally print a fixed '...waiting for owner email at the terminal' line to /dev/tty before the read.
open_findings.observed: ownerEmail() runs bash `read -r -s -p "Owner email (not echoed): " value </dev/tty`. bash writes the -p prompt to STDERR. The driver spawns it with spawnSync default stdio, so stderr is a captured pipe, and the driver itself runs under execFile in tools/agent/lib/proof-orchestrator.mjs:28-31, which also captures (and discards) stderr and prints stdout only after exit. The prompt therefore never reaches the owner's terminal. Reproduced with that exact chain under a pty: the typed value is read (18 chars), but the terminal transcript contains no 'Owner email' prompt. Positive control: the same read with stderr inherited shows the prompt. The owner's `prove --owner` terminal sits silent with no indication that input is wanted. An owner who types the email before the silent read begins has it echoed to the screen and scrollback, because the terminal is still in echo mode.

regression_proof.description: A pty test driving the real two-level chain (Coordinator execFile, then driver spawnSync) asserts that the prompt text appears on the terminal before input and that the returned email length is correct, with nothing echoed.

open_findings.expected: CANDIDATE-AND-PHASES: `npm run agent -- prove TASK_ID` for the claimed task, with required phases derived from the gate manifest and that task's gates. OWNER-ARTIFACT: detect whether owner-artifact R1b/R1c proof is required.
open_findings.minimal_repair: Accept any TASK_ID that is IMPLEMENTING or FIX_REQUIRED, claimed in this worktree by its recorded builder. Pass the id to the driver so the checkpoint line names it, and allowlist a task-id pattern instead of the literal. Map the task's required_gates to phases (gate:static to static, gate:server to server, gate:db to db and residue) and require recovery and owner R1b/R1c only when the task's gates or the manifest demand them, failing closed on unknown gates.
open_findings.observed: proveTask refuses any id other than the literal 'COORD-PROOF-001' (`if (id !== 'COORD-PROOF-001' ...)`), and requires state IMPLEMENTING or FIX_REQUIRED. The owner action printed by the driver (apps/os/scripts/proof-orchestrator.mjs:207) and the allowlist regex (tools/agent/lib/proof-orchestrator.mjs:9) also hardcode COORD-PROOF-001, and the doc says the command 'operates only on COORD-PROOF-001'. Once this task is promoted, `prove` cannot run for any task. The driver also ignores the task's gates: it always runs static, server, db, residue, fixture and the owner R1b/R1c, so it neither derives phases from task gates nor detects whether owner-artifact proof is required. It always checkpoints when R1b/R1c receipts are absent.

regression_proof.description: Tests: prove accepts a second synthetic task id and prints that id in the owner action; a task with only typecheck/gate:static runs no server, db or owner phase; an unknown gate name is refused.

open_findings.expected: The focused tests named in ADVERSARIAL-TESTS, with synthetic inputs and disposable targets.
open_findings.minimal_repair: Give prove() injectable seams (runner, clock-free receipt checker, env reader, prompt) and add tests for each case above, plus gate-proof tests for verify-phase and verify-recovery rejecting other-tree, tampered and missing receipts and accepting a valid exact-tree set.
open_findings.observed: ADVERSARIAL-TESTS lists mandatory coverage. The new tests cover environment planning and isolation, the output allowlist, the gate summary, v2/v3 contract selection, artifact selection, parseLocalEnv, and claim/actor refusal. Nothing exercises the prove() state machine or the new gate-proof.mjs commands (gate-proof.test.ts is unchanged). Not covered: a changed tree between phases stopping the run; a stale, other-tree or tampered receipt being re-run rather than reused by verify-phase or verify-recovery; missing phase evidence blocking READY TO FREEZE; a DB, residue, recovery or R1c-cleanup failure blocking READY; exact-tree idempotence (a second run reuses all receipts and executes nothing); and owner checkpoint refusal and resume with exactly one owner action.

regression_proof.description: Each listed case has a test that fails when its guard (sameCandidate, receiptValid re-check, residue throw, cleanup throw, checkpoint return) is removed.

required_manual_checks.description: Before implementation, inspect Coordinator, gate, manifest, recovery, and R1c code. Add a short tracked architecture note with the deterministic orchestration state machine, resume/idempotence rules, fail-closed transitions, fully automatic steps, explicit owner checkpoints, and proof that no new authority is introduced.

Implement npm run agent -- prove TASK_ID or a freeze-integrated equivalent. Verify a clean claimed worktree and exact candidate SHA/tree before, between, and after phases. Derive required phases from the gate manifest and task gates. Keep direct individual gate commands usable. Static receipts may be recorded before later phases, but aggregate must remain final and fail closed.

Prepare the sanctioned server and DB test environments automatically from already-authorized local inputs only. Prove correct test identity and endpoint selection, no migration or hardening credentials, no recovery secrets in DB/server children, and read-only residue/cleanup verification. Failure or dirty residue prevents completion. Do not access production outside existing sanctioned test behavior.

Run fixture recovery from a truly empty child environment, excluding inherited NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and every PG, DATABASE_URL, Supabase, and recovery-incompatible variable. Preserve the existing recovery runner, network guard, phase separation, artifact and key handling, and fail-closed refusals. DB and recovery authorities must never share a process environment.

Detect whether owner-artifact R1b/R1c proof is required. Select only a sanctioned artifact by pinned repository evidence and validate it without revealing contents. Distinguish v2 from v3: resolve a v2 artifact to its exact pinned legacy contract; let v3 carry its own contract; reject ambiguous or unknown cases. Copy and byte-verify the retained PostgreSQL 17.x build into a private disposable R1c root when required, run both existing R1c legs, and clean up stopped local clusters/root.

Stop only for silent owner email or other explicitly owner-only material, present one action, and resume mechanically after it. Never put owner input in argv, shell history, logs, events, result objects, or serialized receipts. Do not impersonate human admin or automatically unblock a BLOCKED task; green aggregate may only make a human unblock eligible.

Verify every receipt against the exact candidate tree, manifest, suite hash, phase, and environment class; tree changes invalidate prior receipts. Reuse only already-recorded receipts that still pass the existing verifier for the identical tree. Missing, skipped, failed, stale, or tampered evidence prevents green aggregate and freeze. Reruns are idempotent where safe.

Use concise allowlisted progress output with per-phase counts and READY TO FREEZE only after green aggregate. No database URLs, passwords, owner email, backup keys, key material, private backup contents, or unfiltered child output may enter terminal output, Coordinator events/results, review manifests, or logs; test failure paths and gate log_tail as well as success paths.

Run focused Coordinator and architecture tests covering server/DB environment preparation, empty recovery environment and inherited NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, owner checkpoint refusal/resume, v2/v3 contract selection, stale or changed-tree receipts, missing phase evidence, DB/recovery/cleanup failure blocking freeze, secret non-disclosure, separated authorities, exact-tree idempotence, and one owner action. Use synthetic credentials, fixture artifacts, and disposable targets only. Run typecheck.

Diff is limited to the listed Coordinator/proof orchestration code, tests, and docs. No Sales behavior, DB tests, manifest classifications, migrations, schema/RLS/grants, deployment, production data mutation, or new credential authority. Freeze and publish the exact candidate for Claude review through Coordinator.
